KP 2. Differentiating a Negative Power Function Using the Constant Multiple Rule
3.?

If y=14x, find dydx.

E
Fri, Oct 2nd @ 11:39 PM|Elapsed: 0:32Correct

We first rewrite the function as y=14x=14x−1.

Then, we apply the constant multiple and power rules:

dydx=ddx(14x−1)=14⋅ddx(x−1)=14⋅(−1)x−1−1=−14x−2=−14x2

KP 3. Differentiating a Sum of Functions Without Constant Factors Using the Sum Rule
7.?

Find f′(x) for f(x)=x2+x−x.

M
Sat, Oct 3rd @ 12:32 PM|Elapsed: 0:59Correct

The function f(x) is the sum of three power functions. So, we apply the sum rule, and we get

f′(x)=ddx(x2+x−x)=ddx(x2)+ddx(x)−ddx(x)=2x(2−1)+1−12x1/2−1=2x+1−12x−1/2=2x−12x+1.

8.?

Find f′(x) for f(x)=x35−1x3.

M
Sat, Oct 3rd @ 12:34 PM|Elapsed: 1:51Correct

The function f(x) is the sum of two power functions. So, we apply the sum rule, and we get

f′(x)=ddx(x35−1x3)=ddx(x3/5)−ddx(x−3)=35x(3/5−1)−(−3)x(−3−1)=35x(−2/5)+3x(−4)=35x25+3x4.

9.?

Calculate dydx for y=5x15−4x8+7x5.

E
Sat, Oct 3rd @ 12:39 PM|Elapsed: 1:49Correct

Here, we apply the addition, constant multiple, and power rules:

dydx=ddx(5x15−4x8+7x5)=ddx(5x15)−ddx(4x8)+ddx(7x5)=5⋅ddx(x15)−4⋅ddx(x8)+7⋅ddx(x5)=5⋅15x(15−1)−4⋅8x(8−1)+7⋅5x(5−1)=75x14−32x7+35x4

10.?

dydx=ddx(7x5−3x2−5x)=ddx(7x5)−ddx(3x2)−ddx(5x)=7⋅ddx(x5)−3⋅ddx(x2)−5⋅ddx(x)=7⋅5x(5−1)−3⋅2x(2−1)−5⋅1=35x4−6x−5
